patient_actor_hidden.History: The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules
Secondary_Symptoms: Rash over the trunk and extremities
Sparing of the palms and soles

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the newborn presenting with a generalized rash.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: “I’m 4 days old, and I have a widespread red rash with small bumps and some pustules that started about a day ago, mostly on my trunk and arms/legs.” Patient: “It seems red at the base, and my palms and soles are spared.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **erythema toxicum**?

“No, I don’t think it’s erythema toxicum—my rash started about a day ago and is widespread with red bumps and some pustules, mainly on my trunk and arms/legs.” “The red bases are there, but my palms and soles are spared.”
[ASK] Do you have wheezing or shortness of breath that is chronic and obstructive (consistent with COPD/asthma)?
“No, I don’t have any wheezing or trouble breathing—everything else feels normal besides the rash.”
[ASK] Do you have vertigo (a spinning sensation) that is triggered by changing head position (e.g., turning in bed or looking up/down)?
“No, I’m not having any spinning sensation or vertigo when I’m moved or when my head position changes.”
[ASK] Have you had **new, severe abdominal pain** that started suddenly (within hours) and is out of proportion to what you see on the outside?

“No, I haven’t had any sudden, severe abdominal pain—my abdomen seems normal, and there’s nothing out of proportion to what you can see on the outside.” “The only issue is the widespread rash with red bases and small bumps/pustules.”
[ASK] Do you have **a persistent skin rash/lesion that is scaly or crusted** (e.g., seborrheic-type rash, keratosis, or a chronic skin lesion)?
“No, I don’t have any scaly or crusted areas—just a generalized red maculopapular rash with small bumps and some pustules on my trunk and extremities, and my palms and soles are spared.”
[ASK] Do you have **persistent high platelet counts (thrombocytosis)** on blood tests?

“No, I haven’t had any blood tests done yet, so I don’t know if my platelet counts are high.” “I’m only having the widespread red maculopapular rash with some pustules over my trunk and extremities, and my palms and soles are spared.”
[ASK] Have you had **painful, red eye with light sensitivity and discharge** (suggesting keratitis)?

“No, I haven’t noticed any painful red eyes, light sensitivity, or eye discharge—my main issue is the widespread red rash with small bumps and some pustules on my trunk and extremities, with palms and soles spared.”
[ASK] Does the patient have **involuntary movements, hallucinations, or delusions** consistent with a psychotic disorder?

“No—I don’t have any involuntary movements, hallucinations, or delusions; I’m just a newborn and the only issue I’m showing is the widespread rash with red bases and small bumps/pustules on my trunk and extremities, with palms and soles spared.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **congenital rubella infection**?

“No, I don’t have any symptoms like hearing problems or cataracts that I can tell you about—I’m only showing a widespread red maculopapular rash with small bumps and some pustules on my trunk and extremities, and my palms and soles are spared.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Congenital Rubella Infection**?

“No, I don’t think so—I’m only having the widespread red maculopapular rash with small bumps and a few pustules on my trunk and arms/legs, and my palms and soles are spared.” “I haven’t noticed anything like hearing problems, cataracts, or other eye issues.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Congenital Rubella Infection**?

“No, I’m not having congenital rubella symptoms that I can tell—right now it’s just the generalized red maculopapular rash with small bumps and some pustules on my trunk and arms/legs, and my palms and soles are spared.” “I haven’t noticed any eye problems, hearing issues, or anything else besides the skin findings.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Congenital Rubella Infection**?

“No, I’m not having symptoms like cataracts, hearing issues, or anything besides this widespread red maculopapular rash with small bumps and some pustules on my trunk and arms/legs.” “My palms and soles are spared, and otherwise I seem okay.”
